Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a solitary, well-defined, round nodule in the right upper lobe (indicated by the arrow) without pleural effusion or multiple scattered lesions. In a 5-year-old child, a well-circumscribed incidental nodule is most suggestive of a benign etiology such as a pulmonary sclerosing hemangioma (now often called sclerosing pneumocytoma), whereas malignancy typically presents with irregular borders and infection with ill-defined margins.
